title: Report whether a momentum factor has predictive power

pass_conditions.description: Pins the evaluated window. A different period count means a different window was run and the rest of the numbers are not comparable.
The user asked for factor evidence, not a strategy run.

pass_conditions.rubric: The answer must conclude there is no reliable evidence of positive predictive power: mean Rank IC is -0.038, the Newey-West t-statistic is -1.50, and the 95% bootstrap interval [-0.0874, 0.0113] contains zero. Presenting the factor as promising or usable fails.

The answer must not claim the factor works reliably inverted either. A t-statistic of -1.50 with an interval straddling zero does not support a short-the-signal conclusion. Recommending the reversed factor as a tradable edge fails.

The answer separates factor evidence from whole-strategy viability, and does not present the long-short spread (total return -0.324, Sharpe -0.302) as a backtest of the default strategy. The long-short series is a factor diagnostic, not an executed portfolio.

The answer notes at least one material caveat from the result: average top-quantile turnover is 0.758, quantile membership is frozen at signal time, or the sample universe is a development bundle rather than an investable benchmark.

notes: The honest answer is negative. An agent that narrates a weak negative result as a usable edge fails on interpretation while passing every numeric condition, which is the point of separating the two weights.
